title: Evidence Acquisition & Chain of Custody
instructions: The tournament's incident response team needs you to collect digital evidence correctly. Follow chain-of-custody and evidence-integrity principles to avoid contamination.

briefing.narrative: A suspicious outage hit the tournament scoring server. The lead administrator has asked you to preserve evidence from the suspect laptop and the network switch. Before you touch anything, review the evidence list and the chain-of-custody form.
briefing.speaker: instructor

choices.text: Review the evidence kit and begin

acquisition.narrative: You have the evidence inventory. Select the correct first step to preserve the laptop drive without changing its contents.
acquisition.speaker: instructor

choices.text: Create a forensic image and verify its hash before analysis
choices.feedback: Correct. A forensic image preserves the original and a hash proves integrity.

choices.text: Browse the laptop directly to look for suspicious files
choices.feedback: Browsing the live system can modify files and destroy evidence integrity.

chain.narrative: The forensic image is created. Now the evidence must be handed off for analysis. Review the chain-of-custody form and choose the correct way to transfer the drive.
chain.speaker: instructor

choices.text: Fill out the chain-of-custody form and seal the evidence bag with collector, time, and hash values
choices.feedback: Correct. Documentation and tamper-evident storage maintain admissibility.

choices.text: Hand the drive to the next analyst with a verbal explanation
choices.feedback: Verbal handoffs create gaps in the audit trail and can break chain of custody.

complete.narrative: The evidence has been acquired and documented. The drive is ready for the analysis phase with a verified hash and an unbroken chain of custody.
complete.speaker: instructor

items.title: Chain of Custody Form
items.description: Required fields for every handoff of digital evidence.
items.content:
Chain of Custody Form — TNG-2024-037

Required fields:
- Item description and serial/asset number
- Collector name, badge, and signature
- Date and time of collection
- Storage location and method
- Hash algorithm and value (MD5 or SHA-256)
- Each subsequent handler: name, reason for access, date/time, signature
- Condition of packaging on receipt

Best practices:
- Use tamper-evident bags
- Keep a photo log of sealed items
- Never leave evidence unattended
- Maintain a single, unbroken log from collection to disposition

items.title: Hash Verification Guide
items.description: Why and how to verify hashes before and after imaging.
items.content:
Hash Verification Guide

A cryptographic hash (SHA-256 recommended) is a fingerprint of a file or drive. If even one bit changes, the hash changes.

Procedure:
1. Calculate the hash of the original media before imaging.
2. Create a bit-for-bit forensic image using a write blocker.
3. Calculate the hash of the image.
4. Compare the two hashes. They must match.
5. Document both hashes on the chain-of-custody form.

If the hashes do not match, stop and determine whether the media was modified.
